parts.gloss: beast-like people or those lacking discrimination

literal: In the ear taste not-perceiving, mouth perception's beast-like people, even if they perish, even if they live, what does it matter?
translation: What does it matter whether they live or die—those beast-like people who only know the taste of the mouth, but have never experienced the relish of the ear?
modern: செவியால் கேட்கும் சுவையை உணராமல், வாயின் சுவையை மட்டுமே உணரும் விலங்கு போன்ற மனிதர்கள், இறந்தால் என்ன, வாழ்ந்தால் என்ன?
explanation: This couplet concludes the chapter on listening by contrasting the refined pleasure of hearing wisdom with the basic physical pleasure of eating. The author uses the word 'taste' (சுவை) for both senses, comparing the 'taste of the ear' (listening to wise words) with the 'taste of the mouth' (eating food). Those who only seek physical nourishment and ignore intellectual growth are described as 'மாக்கள்' (beast-like people). The couplet bluntly asks what difference it makes to the world whether such unthinking people live or die, as their lives lack any meaningful purpose.
